facts.value: Horses exhibit a diverse array of coat colors and distinctive markings, described by a specialized vocabulary.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: A horse is classified first by its coat color, before breed or sex.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: White markings and various spotting patterns are inherited separately from coat color.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Many genes that create horse coat colors and patterns have been identified.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Current genetic tests can identify at least 13 different alleles influencing coat color.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Research continues to discover new genes linked to specific traits.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: The basic coat colors of chestnut and black are determined by a gene controlled by the Melanocortin 1 receptor.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Its recessive form is 'red' (chestnut) and its dominant form is black.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Additional genes control suppression of black color to point coloration that results in a bay, spotting patterns such as pinto or leopard, dilution genes such as palomino or dun, as well as greying.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Horses that have a white coat color are often mislabeled; a horse that looks 'white' is usually a middle-aged or older gray.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Grays are born a darker shade, get lighter as they age, but usually keep black skin underneath their white hair coat.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: The only horses properly called white are born with a predominantly white hair coat and pink skin.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: Different and unrelated genetic factors can produce white coat colors in horses, including several different alleles of dominant white and the sabino-1 gene.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick

facts.value: There are no 'albino' horses, defined as having both pink skin and red eyes.
facts.programme_association: Equine Science - BSc | University of Limerick
